title: What If the Dead Sea Dried Up? It's Dropping a Meter Every Year

scenes.text: What if the Dead Sea dried up? It's already happening, and the ground is caving in.
Every year the water drops more than a meter. Since 1960 the lake has lost about a third of its surface.
The Jordan River that fed it is diverted to farms and cities, and factories pump out its minerals. A billion cubic meters lost every year.
Retreating water leaves salt underground. Floods dissolve it, and the land collapses. Thousands of sinkholes, some ten meters deep.
A spa built on the shore now sits three kilometers from the water. Scientists expect the drop to last at least a hundred years.
But it won't vanish. The smaller it gets, the saltier it gets, and the slower it evaporates. Smaller, saltier, still there.

description:
What if the Dead Sea dried up? Its level is already falling by more than a meter a year.
The Jordan River is diverted, mineral factories pump the brine, and the lake has lost about a third of its surface since 1960, leaving thousands of sinkholes along the shore. Scientists expect the decline to last at least a century, but a saltier lake evaporates more slowly, so the Dead Sea should stabilize rather than disappear.
